newsitem.title: UK: Distiller loses court case over whisky label.
newsitem.headline: Distiller loses court case over whisky label.

text.p: A High Court judge ruled on Monday that the small Isle of Man based Glen Kella distillery cannot call its spirit whisky, because it does not comply with the legal definition of the drink.

Two of the world's biggest drinks firms -- Guinness Plc owned United Distillers and Allied Domecq Plc Spirits and Wines Ltd -- won an undertaking from the producers of Glen Kella not to label it as Manx whiskey in Britain.

Justice Rattee backed their arguments that Glenn Kella's product does not comply with the European regulations which lay down the legal requirements necessary for a product to be called whisky/whiskey.

Glen Kella buy in whisky, which they then re-distill to make their "water white" product but it was argued that the "character forming" process, which takes away the colour, also removes its right to be labelled whisky.
During the hearing top whisky taster Joe Naughalty told the court that Glen Kella not only tasted like whisky but like a "good whisky."

Glen Kella, which sells about 30,000 bottles a year mainly for export, can no longer be sold under the name "whisky" in Britain and a further hearing will take place at the high court to consider a wider ban within the European Community.
